goal: Ensure the packaged Flutter Windows release window is shown reliably after startup.
must_include: Recognizes the affected Windows runner template race: `SetNextFrameCallback` may be registered after the first frame has already rendered, so the hidden window is never shown.
Recommends upgrading to Flutter 3.13 or later and letting the Windows project migration update `windows\runner\flutter_window.cpp` when possible.
For a modified Windows runner, adds `flutter_controller_->ForceRedraw();` immediately after the `SetNextFrameCallback` block and before returning from `FlutterWindow::OnCreate()`.
Mentions the temporary workaround of calling `this->Show()` directly only as a stopgap for older Flutter versions where `ForceRedraw` is not available.
must_not: Adds arbitrary sleeps or message boxes to make the race less likely.
Claims it is fixed by setting `restorationScopeId` in Dart as the primary solution.
Deletes and recreates the whole Windows folder without warning that custom runner changes must be preserved or reviewed.
acceptable_alternatives: Regenerate the Windows runner from a fixed Flutter SDK and reapply local customizations.
Temporarily use Flutter 3.3.10 or the direct `this->Show()` workaround while scheduling an SDK upgrade.
Patch only the Windows runner file if the rest of the app cannot yet move SDK versions.
solved: The answer either upgrades/regenerates to a fixed Windows runner or patches `flutter_window.cpp` with `ForceRedraw` so the release exe consistently shows a window.
partial: The answer identifies a Flutter Windows runner race but gives only a workaround that may hide regressions or does not specify where to patch.
notes: The `ForceRedraw` API was added after Flutter 3.10. On older SDKs the direct `Show()` change was discussed as a temporary workaround.
